question: How much H2 and CH4 (mg/g) did epoxy resin give in molten KOH at 400 °C?
rendered:
<document title="Dissolution and gasification behavior of thermosetting resin in molten alkali hydroxide">

=== page 1 ===
- Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) and potassium hydroxide (KOH) were mixed in weight ratios of 1 : 0, 3 : 1, 1 : 1, 1 : 3, and 0 : 1 to prepare alkali hydroxide with various Na and K ratios, and then the sample (0.22 g) was added into a cylindrical reactor together with each alkali hydroxide, heated at 150–350 °C for approximately 10 min and maintained at the target temperature for 60 min (total heating time: 70 min).
- For all mixing ratios of alkali hydroxides, polyurethane and epoxy resins were almost completely decomposed at higher than 300 °C. Polyurethane decomposed at a lower temperature than epoxy resin, and phenolic resin was hardly decomposed.
- The highest amounts of organic carbon dissolved from polyurethane and epoxy resin were 508 mg g^−1 at 250 °C and 427 mg g^−1 at 300 °C, respectively.
- Epoxy resin was heated at 500 °C to promote gasification of hydrogen and methane.

=== page 3 ===
- For case (1), epoxy resin (1 g) was immersed in KOH (25.5 g) and heated at 300 °C for 1 h to dissolve organic carbon completely.
- Aer heating, the reactor was cooled to room temperature, and heated to 500 °C for 1 h to promote gasication.

The answer is: At 400 °C, the epoxy resin gave 98.8 mg/g of H2 and 39.6 mg/g of CH4.
